reason: The hypothesis directly mirrors the findings of the single cited paper (E1, E2), which explicitly reports achieving ~2 GPa true stress and ~35% uniform elongation via phase-selective recrystallization in a eutectic high-entropy alloy. The cited evidence supports all key premises, including the microstructural mechanism and the quantitative performance claims, with no misrepresentation.
premises: Phase-selective recrystallization (PSR) can fully recrystallize the soft FCC phase while preserving the hard B2 skeletal morphology in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
PSR eliminates weak boundaries in the soft phase, minimizing early crack nucleation.
Preserving the hard B2 skeleton maintains load-bearing capacity and optimizes strain partitioning.
The PSR microstructure fully activates strain hardening in both phases, leading to simultaneous high strength and ductility.
The specific outcome of ~2 GPa true stress and ~35% uniform elongation is achievable via PSR.
